p.src: Hearing this, Francis said good-bye—and said nothing more. He was ashamed to acknowledge it to himself, but he felt an irresistible curiosity to know what would happen when Agnes arrived at the hotel. Besides, “Mrs. James” had reposed a confidence in him. He got into his gondola, respecting the confidence of “Mrs. James.”

p.src: Towards evening on the third day, Lord Montbarry and his travelling companions arrived, punctual to their appointment.

u.src: Towards evening on the third day, Lord Montbarry and his travelling companions arrived, punctual to their appointment.

p.src: “Mrs. James,” sitting at the window of her room watching for them, saw the new Lord land from the gondola first. He handed his wife to the steps. The three children were next committed to his care. Last of all, Agnes appeared in the little black doorway of the gondola cabin, and, taking Lord Montbarry’s hand, passed in her turn to the steps. She wore no veil. As she ascended to the door of the hotel, the Countess (eyeing her through an opera-glass) noticed that she paused to look at the outside of the building, and that her face was very pale.
